examples.scenario: Smishing attack where a user receives an SMS message impersonating their bank, containing a short URL that redirects to a phishing site designed to steal bank credentials and prompt installation of a malicious Android app.

technical_data.url_obfuscation: The phishing URL uses a domain resembling the legitimate bank (bankxyz.com) but adds 'login-' prefix and '-secure' suffix to the domain. The URL uses HTTP (not HTTPS) and is delivered via a shortened bit.ly URL to hide the final destination. The malicious APK download link is hosted on a separate domain (malicious-domain.com) with an .apk file to trick mobile users into installing malware.

examples.detection_method: Correlation of SMS logs with suspicious URLs, detection of bit.ly to suspicious domain redirection via DNS and HTTP logs, monitoring for HTTP requests to non-HTTPS bank lookalike domains, detection of APK download attempts from unknown domains on mobile endpoints, and email gateway filtering for spoofed sender domains and unusual sending IPs. Mobile security applications can identify malicious APK hash and block installation. Network IDS can alert on HTTP 301 redirects from known URL shorteners to suspicious domains.
relevant_mitre_techniques: T1071.001 - Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
T1110.003 - Brute Force: Password Spraying (if credentials are tested)
